summary: Full backend + frontend test of EzySlot AI MVP. 27 pytest cases pass (auth, public detect/enquiry, isolation, cameras/slots CRUD, live occupancy, history, tickets, stats/health, enquiry convert, fare/service, WebSocket good+bad token). Frontend UI verified end-to-end: landing + Try Detection (real YOLOv8 count returned), enquiry form present, /login with demo buttons, client /app live monitor renders SlotCanvas polygons + FREE/OCCUPIED/UNKNOWN chips + nearest-free banner + WS status LIVE + camera switcher works, History/Support/Service tabs functional, developer /ops KPI cards + fleet occupancy donut + telemetry cards + all nav pages present, Add Client dialog creates client.

minor.issue: Bad-token WebSocket connection is rejected via ingress HTTP 403 handshake rather than server-side custom close code 4401. Behavior is still secure (connection is rejected), but frontend cannot distinguish 4401 from generic 403. Consider returning 401 status from handshake or a policy-violation close code.

issues: Radix DialogContent missing aria-describedby / DialogDescription — accessibility warning in console, not a functional bug.

action_items: (Optional) Return an explicit HTTP 401 (or custom 4401 close) for bad-token WebSocket so frontend can surface auth errors distinctly.
(Optional) Add DialogDescription / aria-describedby to Radix Dialogs to silence a11y warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 807 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline; split into modules (routers/auth, routers/cameras, routers/tickets, realtime/, seed.py) for maintainability.

CORS is set to allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False; fine for Bearer-only auth, but cookies (httponly access_token) will be blocked by browsers under credential-less CORS. Frontend uses Bearer so no impact today.
/api/files/{path} accepts an `auth` query param and Authorization header but never validates them — the annotated image is effectively public. If detection output must be private, enforce auth here.
occupancy_loop uses random status flips (simulated) — acceptable for MVP demo but should be documented as demo data; not driven by actual YOLO on live camera feeds.
seed() early-returns if any clients exist, so schema/slot changes on redeploy won't be re-seeded — expected but worth noting for ops.
